newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to destroy 20-30,000 pigs in fever outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to destroy 20-30,000 pigs in fever outbreak.

text.p: The Dutch Agriculture Ministry said Thursday it would order the destruction all the pigs within a two kilometre radius of two reported swine fever outbreaks, a measure which could involve 20,000 to 30,000 pigs.
The first outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands since 1992 was discovered Tuesday at a farm in the south of the country, with the second reported Thursday at another farm 1.5 kilometres away.
"All the pigs within a two kilometre radius of these two farms will be destroyed," a ministry spokeswoman said. "That might concern as many as 30,000 pigs," she added.

The transport of all animals, apart from poultry, would be banned within a 12-kilometre radius of the two farms in a move that exceeded EU disease management regulations calling for a 10-kilometre transport embargo, the spokeswoman said.

Around 1,700 pigs at the first farm and 900 pigs at the second had been or were about to be destroyed, while three abattoirs which had handled pigs from the farms recently had been shut down and the meat from them destroyed.
"We're still carrying out blood tests in the area. This is a very dangerous disease and it can spread very quickly, but we're hoping it has been contained," she said.
Earlier, a ministry spokesman said it was too early to say if there would be any restrictions imposed on exports.

Germany earlier this week prohibited the export of pigs for slaughter from four German states after an outbreak of swine fever. Authorities have ordered the slaughter of over 14,000 pigs to contain it but Belgium and Switzerland have announced restrictions on German imports of live pigs and pork meat.
U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it was monitoring the Dutch outbreak but would not impose any trade restrictions yet. --Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
